G L E U H R
Wellness Pvt Ltd
CLINIC COUNSELLOR
Role · KRAs · KPIs · SOP · Consequences
Reports to: Branch Manager  ·  Functional line: Manisha (Head of Sales)

1  ·  Role Purpose
The Clinic Counsellor is the commercial heart of the branch. Every other function — reception, doctors, therapists, marketing — exists to make sure a client walks into the counsellor's cabin. What happens in the next thirty to forty minutes after she sits down is what decides whether GLEUHR earns a new client or watches her walk out.

In one sentence.  Sell honestly. Hold the client afterwards. Both. Neither alone is enough.

Reporting structure
Reports to: Branch Manager (line)
Functional line: Manisha (Head of Sales)
Escalation chain (per playbook): BM → Team Leader → Manisha. Never skip the chain.
For hard-line violations or distress: Harman (Head of Departments) or Founder — directly.

2  ·  Key Result Areas (KRAs)
Four KRAs. Each carries weight in monthly review.
KRA 1 — Convert
Run the six-step playbook on every consultation. Every step, in order.
Convert consultations into packages at the branch's target rate
Quote per package, never just the total. Calculate in front of the client.
Use the one-shot offer only as a closer — never as an opener
Handle all seven brand-approved objections using the brand-approved scripts

KRA 2 — Hold
Follow up with every client according to the route — balance pending, balance clear, or only-consultation
Make every committed follow-up call — real call, ≥ 30 seconds, logged in CRM
Maintain a worried-about-clients list. Call them unprompted.
Meet every client after her treatment session — not just before
Run honest upsell and cross-sell conversations — the ones that don't damage trust

KRA 3 — Document
Every consultation logged in CRM with: session, plan, products, follow-up date, amount
Every product dispensed has 'Product explained' ticked + confirmation note
Every complaint logged in the register within 1 hour. BM informed same day.
Every call (follow-up, callback, escalation) logged with a one-line summary

KRA 4 — Stand by the brand
Never break a hard-line violation (eight listed below)
Stay inside the brand-approved scripts on guarantees, expectations, and discounts
Escalate when you cannot resolve — never improvise
Protect client privacy — never discuss one client to another, never leave the cabin during sensitive conversation

3  ·  Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)
Five KPIs. Reviewed monthly with BM. Functional review with Manisha quarterly.

The five core Counsellor KPIs
KPI
What it measures
Reviewed by
Conversion into package
% of consultations that convert into a paid package
BM + Manisha
Total revenue
Monthly closed revenue from counsellor's consultations
BM + Manisha
Overall conversion rate
End-to-end lead → revenue conversion for leads handled
BM + Manisha
Upsell / Cross-sell
% of active clients upgraded or cross-sold into additional services
BM + Manisha
Follow-up discipline
Committed follow-ups completed on time + worried-about clients held + post-treatment client meetings
BM

Why follow-up discipline is a core KPI.  We are not a clinic that closes and disappears. The brand is built on the client feeling held — through the treatment, through doubts, through results that come slower than she hoped. A counsellor with high conversion and low follow-up discipline is doing damage that takes the brand months to repair. The two KPIs are not separate. They are the same job.

4  ·  Standard Operating Procedure
The SOP is the six-step playbook (see separate Counsellor Playbook document v1.0). Summary here. Detailed scripts in the playbook.

Step 1 — Rapport
Open the door. Smile. Greet by name. Seat her. Tea / coffee / water.
Six rapport questions: profession, location, medical history, previous treatment, skincare history, what brought her in
Spend 5-7 minutes here. Do not jump to her skin concern in the first 5 minutes.

Step 2 — Diagnose
Name the concern confidently — no 'shayad', 'thoda', 'actually'
Explain why it happened, tied to her context
Testimonial validation — specific past patient, similar profile
Present the inside-out solution path

Step 3 — Treatment Process
Internal track — diet (always recommend 6 months)
External track — customised serum + doctor-led sessions
Frame: '14 sessions but only 5-7 visits — multiple sessions per visit'

Step 4 — Discuss Package
Lead with the breakdown — pick up the calculator, punch numbers in front of her
Quote per package, never just the total
Anchor the discount to her booking — 'Nitasha called specially for you'
Read her face — lean back = processing, lean in = engaged, arms crossed = address resistance
Never disclose after-discount or one-shot amount without engagement signal
If she asks for more discount: hold the line first, then BM call only after her yes-conditional

Step 5 — Handle Objections
Seven brand-approved objection scripts. Use the line — adapt the tone. Do not invent.
Diet plan not needed ("healthy lifestyle already")
Distance objection ("main door se hoon")
Family discussion ("family se discuss karna hai")
Price objection ("bahut mehnga hai")
Comparison with another clinic
Trust issue / past experience
Guarantee question ("kya guarantee hai?")

Step 6 — Close + Assurance + Follow-up
Lock payment mode. Process via CRM only — no off-system payments, ever
Assurance message at end of every conversion — 'ab humari responsibility hai aap ka result'
First-day handoff: walk her to doctor, confirm products, confirm dietitian connect, lock next visit in CRM
Three follow-up routes — balance pending, balance clear, only-consultation

5  ·  Hard-Line Violations  ·  Termination Track
These override your score.  Any one of the eight = same-day review by Head of Audit. Score becomes irrelevant. Consequence is termination track. Read carefully. Internalise.

#
Violation
Why it matters
1
Off-system payment collected (personal UPI/GPay/QR/cash to own account)
Brand and legal integrity — even if client offers, even if BM informally suggests
2
Outright outcome guarantee ('100% results', 'guaranteed cure')
Legally and ethically dangerous. The line is 'acche results' — never guarantee.
3
Floor-breach pricing (quoting below BM-authorised floor)
Destroys margin discipline; one breach forces every other counsellor to follow
4
Discount disclosed before yes (revealing one-shot or lower number too early)
Once the floor is revealed, the anchor cannot be rebuilt
5
Fake conversion or inflated entry in CRM
Breaks the data the company runs on; impossible to recover trust after
6
Cross-clinic lead poaching or different prices at different clinics for same lead
Destroys regional discipline and undermines colleagues
7
Privacy breach (discussing one client to another, sharing photos, etc.)
Legal and reputational risk; clients lose trust in the entire brand
8
Disconnecting / walking out on a client mid-consultation
Brand promise violated; one incident becomes a permanent story

If you feel about to do any of these — STOP.  Call the BM. Step out of the cabin. The 90 seconds you spend escalating is the 90 seconds that saves your job.

7  ·  Authority and Escalation
What the counsellor decides without escalation
How to run the consultation — within the six-step playbook
Which testimonial to use, in what tone, with which client
Diet plan recommendation (3 vs 6 month — always recommend 6 but client chooses)
Whether to push for one-shot or accept installment
Follow-up cadence within the route guideline

What needs BM sign-off
Any discount below the standard published offer
Refund requests
Difficult client situations — angry, threatening, demanding
Cabin reassignment (if a consultation runs long)
First-time exceptions to any step of the playbook

What needs Team Leader / Manisha
Cross-clinic or cross-region issues
Policy questions (what the brand allows, what it doesn't)
Anything BM cannot resolve

What comes to Harman / Founder directly
Pressure from anyone (BM, peer, client) to break a hard-line violation
Serious client complaint with reputational risk
Anything that feels structurally wrong

8  ·  Consequences Framework
Trigger
Response
Single-month miss on a KPI
Documented in 1-on-1 with BM; cause analysis; corrective plan agreed
Two consecutive months miss on the same KPI
Written notice; 30-day improvement plan with weekly check-ins
Three consecutive months miss
Formal Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) with HR
Single hard-line violation
Same-day review by Head of Audit; termination track
Pattern of low follow-up discipline (closing without holding)
Written warning; functional review with Manisha
Repeated complaints about counsellor behaviour
Investigation; corrective coaching or termination depending on severity

9  ·  What 'Good' Looks Like — End of First Year

Conversion into package consistently at or above target every month.
Total revenue trending upward each quarter.
Follow-up discipline at 95%+ — meaning the clients you close, you hold.
Upsell/cross-sell happening naturally — the clients you sold a package to are upgrading because they trust you, not because they were pushed.
Zero hard-line violations.
Clients who request you by name when they return. Other clients referred by their friends.

The ultimate test.  When the founder asks your BM 'who do you trust most with a difficult consultation?' — your name is on the list. That is what a good counsellor at GLEUHR looks like.
